question: Are snapshots vaulted to Cohesity FortKnox immutable by default, and what mechanism enforces it?
gold_facts: Snapshots vaulted in a FortKnox cloud vault are DataLocked by default.
DataLock makes storage WORM-compliant so backups and archives cannot be tampered with or deleted.
FortKnox uses AWS S3 Object Lock as the DataLock mechanism.

A.text: Yes. Snapshots vaulted in a cloud vault are DataLocked by default, making them immutable [1][3]. DataLock makes storage WORM-compliant so backups and archives cannot be tampered with or deleted, preventing ransomware attacks [1][4]. The mechanism enforcing this is AWS S3 Object Lock, which Cohesity FortKnox uses to DataLock the snapshots [1].

documents.title: DataLock
documents.text:
DataLock
DataLock

DataLock enables your storage to be WORM-compliant. When it is enabled, your data such as backups and archives cannot be tampered or deleted. This results in prevention from ransomware attacks on your data. By default, the snapshots vaulted in a cloud vault are DataLocked. Cohesity FortKnox uses AWS S3 Object Lock as the mechanism to DataLock the snapshots.

documents.title: Get Started
documents.text:
Get Started

Before you start on Cohesity FortKnox, it is important that you plan and decide on aspects such as:

- l Data from which cluster(s) should be vaulted in the cloud?
- l Which workloads such as Virtual Machines and Databases should be vaulted to the cloud?
- l In which Amazon Web Services region should the cloud vault be created?
- l How long do you want to retain the snapshots in a cloud vault?
- l Do you want to use Cohesity-managed key management service (KMS) or Selfmanaged KMS?

Note: Self-managed KMS option supports only Amazon Web Services KMS.

- l What would be the backup window ?

Cohesity Clusters
Cohesity FortKnox vaults data from your cluster to the cloud. To achieve this, it's important for you to plan and decide on the clusters whose data will be sent to a cloud vault. After you decide on the clusters, you have to ensure that these clusters are associated with the Cohesity Helios account that includes Cohesity FortKnox. For more information on the supported cluster types, see Clusters.

Workloads
Cohesity FortKnox allows you to recover workloads such as virtual machines and databases. For more information, see Supported Workloads, Clusters, and Regions.

For more information on workflows that are supported for each workload, see Supported Workflows.

Snapshot Retention
The snapshots that are vaulted in the cloud vault are DataLocked by default and can be deleted after the retention period. Before you start using Cohesity FortKnox, It's important that you decide on how long you want to retain the snapshots in a cloud vault.

documents.title: Edit Policies
documents.text:
Edit Policies
Edit Policies

In Cohesity FortKnox, you can edit the policies that are available in the Cohesity clusters associated with the Cohesity Data Cloud user account and add Cloud Vault configurations to policies.

A policy is a reusable set of settings that define how and when objects are protected, replicated and vaulted. You select which standard policy to use when configuring a Protection Group. A Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured, vaulted or replicated.

You can use the default standard policies or create your own custom policies.

Tip: Policies eliminate the effort to repetitively define the same settings for different sources and protection groups and therefore, saves time for you.

Note: When a policy includes a Cloud Vault, Smart Retention Adjustment protects your local backups from being deleted before your data is safely copied to its secondary target. If a Cloud Vault (or Replication or Archive) task is cancelled or fails after a successful local backup, Smart Retention Adjustment extends the retention of the local copy to match the failed target's retention. Smart Retention Adjustment is enabled by default. For more information, see Smart Retention Adjustment.

Follow the steps below to add Cloud Vault protection to a policy.

1. In FortKnox , navigate to Cloud Vaults > Protection .
2. The Activity tab on the Protection page appears.
2. (Optional) Filter the list of policies for Cluster and Target Type , and add the required columns from the icon.
3. Under the Policy column, select the policy name and select Edit .
5. The Edit Protection Policy page appears.
4. Select Add Cloud Vault .
7. The Cloud Vault card appears.
5. You have to provide the following details.
- a. Transfer to : Lists the cloud vaults that are available for archiving.
- b. Every : Specify the time interval at which the data should be vaulted to the cloud vault.
- c. Retain for xx days : Specify how long the snapshots will be retained in the Cloud Vault.
- d. Data Locked : By default, the data in a Cloud Vault is data locked. Data Lock enables your storage to be WORM-compliant. When it is enabled, your data such as backups and archives cannot be tampered or deleted. This results in prevention from ransomware attacks.
- e. Smart Retention Adjustment : Enabled by default. When enabled, if the Cloud Vault task is cancelled or fails after the local backup succeeds, the retention of the local copy is automatically extended to the Cloud Vault's retention.
- f. Transfer only successful runs : Select this option if you want only the successful protection runs to be sent to a Cloud Vault
6. Select Save .

The Activity tab on the Protection page appears.
3. (Optional) Filter the list of policies for Cluster and Target Type, and add the required columns from the icon.

b. Every: Specify the time interval at which the data should be vaulted to the cloud vault.
c. Retain for xx days: Specify how long the snapshots will be retained in the Cloud Vault.
d. Data Locked: By default, the data in a Cloud Vault is data locked. Data Lock enables your storage to be WORM-compliant. When it is enabled, your data such as backups and archives cannot be tampered or deleted. This results in prevention from ransomware attacks.
e. Smart Retention Adjustment: Enabled by default. When enabled, if the Cloud Vault task is cancelled or fails after the local backup succeeds, the retention of the local copy is automatically extended to the Cloud Vault's retention.

B.text: Yes. Snapshots vaulted in the Cohesity FortKnox cloud vault are DataLocked by default [2], and DataLock is enabled by default for backups to Cloud Vault, preventing data deletion until expiry [3]. The enforcement mechanism is AWS S3 Object Lock, which FortKnox uses to DataLock the snapshots [1].

documents.title: Prerequisites
documents.text:
[Prerequisites › Prerequisites]
1. Transfer to : Choose a cloud vault where you want to transfer or backup your data.
2. Every : Choose either Run or any time interval to determine how often data should be backed up to a Cloud Vault. This defines the protection schedule for capturing backups.
3. Retain for : Specify for how many days the backups are retained in a Cloud Vault.
4. l For AWS, the minimum retention allowed is 30 days for warm vault and 90 days for cold vault.

- l For Azure, the minimum retention allowed is 30 days for warm vault and 120 days for cold vault.

You can configure different retention time for different policies. For Free Trial users, the retention period is set to 30 days.

Note: By default, DataLock is enabled for backups to Cloud Vault. This means the data cannot be deleted once it is sent to the vault till it expires. After the expiry date, the data will be automatically removed.

4. You can optionally choose to Transfer only successful runs .
5. Select Add .
6. On the Cloud Vault Protection page, select Continue .

The Cloud Vault Quorum Group page appears.

You've added Cloud Vault Protection to the policy in your cluster. The vaulting task to the cloud vault is initiated in the next protection run.

Note: You can view the vault added to the policy from the Cohesity Data Cloud (Self-managed), however, you cannot modify it. Vaulting can be configured only from the Policies tab in the Protection page in Cohesity FortKnox.

## Create Cloud Vault Quorum Group

In Cohesity FortKnox, you can define a group of users called a quorum group who can collectively decide whether the operations initiated by a FortKnox user are allowed to be executed or not.

Follow the steps below to create a quorum group.

1. Select Create Quorum Group .
2. Under Group Details , enter the Name of the quorum group, choose an Operation Target , and add a Description (Optional).
3. Under Operations , Recover from FortKnox Vault and Recover Metadata from FortKnox Vault are selected by default.

Note: An operation can be assigned to only one quorum group. This means an operation, for example, Recover from FortKnox Vault , can be approved by only one Quorum group.

4. Under Approvers , add the members of the quorum group. The list of members are populated based on the users available in your Cohesity Data Cloud account.
5. Set the Approval Quorum . You can either select All Members or set a minimum value of members required to approve any requests.
6. Set Approval Workflow . You can enter a time value after which the defined action, either Accept or Deny , will be taken automatically.
7. Select Create . You've created the quorum group.
8. Select Complete .

The Dashboard page appears.

You've now successfully completed the onboarding steps to access Cohesity FortKnox .

question: How many Cohesity FortKnox cloud vaults can I create in one region, and what do I need in order to use cold storage vaults?
gold_facts: Up to 10 cloud vaults can be created in a region, with a name chosen at creation.
A cloud vault's storage class can be Warm or Cold.
Cold storage cloud vaults require the FortKnox Cold Vault entitlement.

A.text:
You can create multiple cloud vaults in a region — up to 10 — and choose a desired name for the vaults during creation [1]. A Region in FortKnox is used to provision one or multiple vaults [3].

To use cold storage vaults, you need the FortKnox Cold Vault entitlement [2]. FortKnox supports storing data to cold storage cloud vaults in addition to existing warm vaults, with a storage class choice of Warm or Cold during creation [4]. Note that only Warm cloud vaults are supported in Microsoft Azure (Cold vaults are not supported) [5]. Cold vaults are available for AWS and GCP, with a minimum retention of 90 days for AWS and 365 days for GCP [10].

sources.paraphrase: Cohesity FortKnox supports creating multiple cloud vaults (up to 10) in a region and allows choosing a desired name for the vaults during creation.

documents.title: March 2023
documents.text:
[March 2023 › March 2023]
## March 2023

## Support for Multiple Cloud Vaults in a Region

You can now create multiple cloud vaults (up to 10) in a region and choose your desired name for the vaults during its creation.


## Support for Cold Storage Cloud Vaults

In addition to the existing warm vaults, you can now store your data to cold storage cloud vaults. While creating a cloud vault, you can choose a storage class, Warm or Cold .

Note: The Cold storage cloud vault is available only if you've purchased FortKnox Cold Vault entitlement. For more information, see Create Cloud Vault.


## Support for New Workloads

Cohesity FortKnox now supports the following workloads.

Note: Instant Volume Mount and Clone operation is not supported for the following workloads. Additionally, Cohesity Agent-based backups, AWS Native snapshots, and Azure Native snapshots are not supported.


- l File-based and VDI-based SQL backups
- l Nutanix Acropolis Hypervisor (AHV)
- l AIX Server

- l Amazon EC2
- l Azure VMs

## Key Concepts

## Cloud Vault

documents.title: Prerequisites
documents.text:
[Prerequisites › Prerequisites]
## Create Cloud Vault

A cloud vault is a destination where you can backup your Cohesity cluster data and recover it to the original or a new location. Once it is created, the data from the cluster is vaulted to the cloud vault.

Follow the steps below to create a cloud vault.

1. On the Welcome to FortKnox page, select Create Cloud Vault
2. .

You can select Cancel to complete the steps later and continue to use Cohesity Data Cloud.

2. On the Create Cloud Vault dialog box, choose a Region .

A Region is used to provision one or multiple vaults.

3. Choose a Storage Class .

Storage class for the vaults can be Warm or Cold for AWS, Warm or Warm LRS (Locally Redundant Storage) or Cold LRS for Azure, and Warm or Cold for GCP. The options available to you are based on your FortKnox entitlements.

1. Warm : A warm vault created on an AWS Region leverages Amazon S3 Standard Infrequent Access (S3-IA), and requires a minimum retention of 30 days. Starting with Cohesity release 7.1.2\_u4, all new vault data is stored in the Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval storage tier.

Similarly, a warm vault created on a Microsoft Azure Region leverages Azure Cool Blob Storage.

A warm vault created on a GCP region leverages GCP Coldline storage and requires a minimum retention of 30 days.

When using any warm vault, the recovery starts immediately upon initiation.

2. Cold : A cold vault created on an AWS Region leverages Amazon S3-Glacier Flexible Retrieval (FR), and requires a minimum retention of 90 days.
2. Similarly, a cold vault created on a GCP Region leverages GCP Archive storage and requires a minimum retention of 365 days.
3. Warm LRS : A warm LRS vault created on a Microsoft Azure Region leverages Azure Cold Blob LRS storage. It requires a minimum retention of 90 days.

Note: Azure Warm LRS is supported only on cluster versions 7.3 and later.

4. Cold LRS : A cold LRS vault created on a Microsoft Azure Region leverages Azure Archive Blob LRS storage. It requires a minimum retention of 180 days.

Note: Azure LRS maintains three copies of data within a single data center in the selected primary region.

4. Choose a key management service from Select Encryption Option . For more information, see Key Management.

Note: Azure and GCP vaults support only Cohesity KMS.

## 5. Click Create .

The provisioning of the cloud vault has started. The selected region is displayed in the list and the status is shown as Provisioning . When the status changes to Provisioned , the map shows a green bubble that signifies the location of the Cloud Vault.

Note: If FortKnox vault provisioning fails, exit the onboarding wizard, go to Vault Configuration, and retry. Vault will provision successfully after some time.

Note: The Clusters column shows the count of paired clusters and the number of clusters associated with the Cohesity Data Cloud account. If the clusters associated with the Cohesity Data Cloud account are not paired completely or partially, then you can reach out to Cohesity Support.

## 6. Select Continue .

The Cloud Vault Protection page appears.

## Add Cloud Vault Protection

On the Cloud Vault Protection page, you have to add the cloud vault protection to the policies that are available in the cluster. The cloud vault protection in a policy defines the cloud vault that will contain the vaulted data, the time interval when the data is sent to the cloud vault, and the retention time for snapshots in the cloud vault.

Follow the steps below to add the cloud vault protection to a policy.

1. Select Add Cloud Vault Protection .
2. Choose a Cluster and a Policy
3. .

The policy details are displayed.

3. Select Continue .

The Add Cloud Vault Protection to Policy appears.

Only Warm cloud vaults are supported for Cohesity FortKnox in Microsoft Azure (Cold vaults are not supported).
